items.stem: What does Intune install on a device during enrollment to enforce organizational policies?

options.rationale: Correct: enrollment installs an MDM certificate that lets Intune enforce policy.
A VPN gateway is not installed during Intune enrollment.
Enrollment does not create a local admin account.
A recovery key is not what enables policy enforcement at enrollment.

items.explanation: Correct: enrollment installs an MDM certificate that lets Intune enforce policy.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Intune device compliance policies are true? (Select TWO.)

options.text: They mark a device as compliant or noncompliant
options.rationale: Correct: compliance evaluation marks devices compliant or noncompliant.

options.text: Conditional Access can use compliance status to allow or block access
options.rationale: Correct: Conditional Access can require a device be marked compliant.

options.text: They physically prevent an operating system from booting
options.rationale: Incorrect: compliance policies do not block the OS from booting.

options.text: They remove the need to enroll devices
options.rationale: Incorrect: compliance status requires the device to be enrolled.

items.explanation: Correct: compliance evaluation marks devices compliant or noncompliant.

items.stem: In compliance policy settings, which option helps ensure only confirmed-compliant devices access resources?

options.text: Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as Not compliant
options.rationale: Correct: this setting treats unassigned devices as noncompliant for Conditional Access.

options.text: Set the validity period to 120 days
options.rationale: Validity period alone does not ensure only compliant devices get access.
Disabling Conditional Access would remove the access control.

options.text: Mark all devices as compliant by default
options.rationale: This weakens security rather than ensuring compliance.

items.explanation: Correct: this setting treats unassigned devices as noncompliant for Conditional Access.
